mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discount rates reducing the present value of future earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or the FEDFUNDS change is not >0.25% in any observed month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL for three consecutive months indicates accelerating inflation, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors discount future cash flows more aggressively.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window with CPIAUCSL decline, the 20-day forward return is positive (p < 0.05) or the inflation signal is not sustained for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PAYEMS (labor market strength) combined with UNRATE below 5% suggests a tight labor market, which drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as firms expand investment in growth.
failure_condition: In tight labor regimes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 60-day historical average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in INDPRO (industrial production) above its 12-month moving average during a period of falling FEDFUNDS is expected to produce a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as growth signals offset rate cuts.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite the combined signal (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (household spending) rises by at least 3% in a month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting optimism about consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >=3% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 6 months of expansionary HOUST, the 5-day forward return is not positive in >70% of months (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (GDP) for two consecutive quarters in a deflationary FEDFUNDS environment is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as weak demand offsets easing rates.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases for 2 consecutive quarters and FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite the combined signal (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS remains flat for two months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to reduced wage growth expectations and muted hiring.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS does not increase for 2 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in >50% of similar regimes (robustness check).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -2% for three consecutive months in a non-stagflation regime is expected to produce a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals contractionary monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not negative when the signal is present (p > 0.05).
